_note: PRIOR parameters for the target model. These are beliefs, not measurements. The target_model.py re-estimates every one of them from the board's own data as soon as mature posts exist, and stamps provenance on the output. Never edit a number here to make a readout look better; the model overwrites them from data.
_posts_per_day_note: The cadence the newsroom plans against. Matches config/account.json cadence_target_posts_per_day. This is a floor, not a goal: volume is the last lever.
_conversion_note: Follows per impression. 0.05%. This is the same reference rate the noise floor uses, so the kill gate and the target model are calibrated against one number, not two.
_discovery_note: Impressions per post that do NOT come from the follower base: algorithmic discovery, search, quote-tweet pickup, browse. For a new account this is the entire reach. Almost certainly wrong in both directions and replaced by measurement.
_follower_share_note: Fraction of the follower base that sees one post, before algorithmic dilution.
_reach_scale_note: The follower count at which the timeline throttles per-post reach by half. This term is what stops the model from compounding forever. It is the single most important unmeasured number in this file: it decides whether growth is exponential or linear, and therefore whether ANY cadence reaches 1M.
_offplatform_cohort_note: Followers injected per week by off-platform distribution: Hacker News, Reddit, Discord, newsletter, large-account replies. Zero at baseline because no channel has run yet. The model solves for the value of this term that would close the gap; that solved value is the off-platform weekly target.
_scenarios_note: The bracket is not decoration. The base case is a belief; the spread is how much the answer moves when the belief is wrong. Any conclusion that flips across the bracket is not a conclusion, and the model says so.
